questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following:

(i) Photosynthesis

(ii) Respiration *(4, 4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Photosynthesis** is the process by which **green plants make carbohydrate (glucose) from carbon dioxide and water, using light energy absorbed by chlorophyll**, and release oxygen as a by-product:

$$6CO_2 + 6H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{light, chlorophyll}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2$$

(ii) **Respiration** is the **chemical breakdown of food substances (usually glucose) in the living cells to release energy** (stored in ATP) for the activities of the organism. In **aerobic respiration** oxygen is used and carbon dioxide and water are produced:

$$C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O + \text{energy}$$

(In anaerobic respiration the breakdown takes place without oxygen and releases less energy.)

questions.enonce_markdown: How is the leaf adapted to carry out its function of photosynthesis? *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The leaf is adapted to absorb light and carbon dioxide and to obtain water for photosynthesis:

1. The **lamina is broad and flat**, giving a **large surface area** to trap light and to absorb carbon dioxide.
2. The lamina is **thin**, so light reaches all the cells and gases diffuse over a **short distance**.
3. The **upper epidermis and the cuticle are thin and transparent**, so that light passes through to the photosynthetic cells (the cuticle is waxy and reduces water loss).
4. The **palisade mesophyll** cells are **tall, closely packed** and contain **many chloroplasts** (with chlorophyll) near the upper surface, where most light is received.
5. The **spongy mesophyll** has **large air spaces** between loosely arranged cells, so that carbon dioxide diffuses easily to the cells and oxygen diffuses out.
6. **Stomata** (mostly on the lower epidermis), each with two **guard cells**, open to let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out, and close to reduce water loss.
7. **Veins** carry **water and mineral salts in the xylem** to the cells and carry away the sugars in the **phloem**; they also support the lamina.
8. The **petiole** and the **arrangement of leaves (leaf mosaic)** place the lamina at right angles to the light, with little overlapping.

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain what happens to the glucose produced during photosynthesis. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The glucose made in the leaf has several fates:

1. **Respiration**: part of it is oxidised in the cells to release **energy** for the life processes of the plant.
2. **Storage as starch**: excess glucose is converted into **insoluble starch** (stored temporarily in the leaf, and for the long term in organs such as roots, tubers, seeds and fruits). Starch is insoluble, so it does not affect the osmotic balance of the cells.
3. **Transport as sucrose**: glucose is changed into **sucrose**, which is **translocated through the phloem** to growing parts (shoot tips, root tips, flowers, fruits) and to storage organs.
4. **Cellulose**: glucose is converted into **cellulose** to build **new cell walls** for growth.
5. **Proteins**: glucose combined with **nitrates** (and sulphur) absorbed from the soil forms **amino acids**, which are built up into **proteins** (also used to make chlorophyll and other substances).
6. **Fats and oils**: some glucose is converted into **fats and oils**, stored for example in seeds and nuts.
7. Some is stored as **sugar** in fruits and in the sap of roots such as beet.
